title: sim-run.test.ts is load-sensitive: tests flake when run beside other files
evidence: Fixed 2026-11-12, tests only (net prod LOC 0). Holders no longer end on a fixed sleep: they run `sh -c until [ -f release ]` and end when the test calls release(); afterEach releases and SIGTERMs anything still running, so a failed test leaks nothing. (1) old-token test (was `sleep 3`): holder now held until after the exit-75 assertion. Same fix for the other holders a loaded machine could outlast: 'makes a second caller wait' (was `sleep 1`; now waits until the second caller prints 'waiting up to', then releases), 'gives up after the wait limit' (`sleep 5`), status 'names the holder' (`sleep 2`), ui-test self-rerun (`sleep 1`), idle 'while a run holds it' (`sleep 8` vs a 7 s wait). (2) demo-device test parses the printed 'Booted for XmYs' age and asserts 125 <= age <= 125 + (seconds status took) + 1, since status runs several fake xcrun calls before reading its clock. Kill-window tests: HR_SIM_KILL_SECONDS 2 -> 5, so the 1 s 'still alive' check has 4 s of slack. Idle 'another run ended since': idle 1 s -> 3 s (the second run must end before the sleeper wakes). Upper bounds widened where the bug they rule out is far beyond: run limit < 8 s -> < 15 s (command is sleep 20); guard+lock cap < 6 s -> < 7 s (the bug takes >= 3 + 4 s); until() caps for shutdown waits 6-8 s -> 15 s; the 3 s `until(() => !busy())` cap -> 10 s. afterEach note: a waiter queued behind a holder that ignores the release file would block cleanup (bash defers SIGTERM while the wrapper waits in lockf). Proof: 3 solo runs + 1 beside ios/scripts/ and tools/codex-review.test.ts, all green; each started at 1-min load under 8, and the combined run's load rose to 25.85 during it.
